parts.part: settlement area (Locality 1 of the main mound; Central, East, North and Northwest Areas)
parts.layout_phase: Period IIA (Mature Harappan), Structural Phase-1, in the final report of 2011; the 2008 interim report (Occasional Paper 6) assigned the exposed street plan to Structural Phase II, 'Late Period II'
parts.what_was_built: A planned Mature Harappan settlement of large mud-brick structure complexes arranged along a main street, smaller streets and lanes, laid out as a parallelogram. The final report states that 'the plan of the Mature Harappan settlement at Farmana appears to have been established during Period-IIA', with 'a main street, small streets and lanes, and massive structural complexes neatly arranged along their margins', and that the pattern 'was established during Period-IIA and continued in IIB without any change' (Shinde et al. 2011: 45); 'elaborate remains of well-planned mud and burnt-brick structural complexes, streets, rectangular fire places and storage areas appear at the beginning of Period-IIA' (p. 40). The fully exposed street and blocks, however, are described in the Period IIB section: Main Street, 3.60 to 4 m wide and traced for 28 m with bullock-cart ruts, Lane no. 1 and Structure Complexes 2, 3 and 4 (pp. 97-153); Structure Complex 2 'lines up with Structure No. 1, which is associated with an early construction phase' (p. 97). All structures are of mud brick in the ratio 1:2:4, with burnt brick for bathing platforms and drains (p. 45). The site was levelled for agriculture, so only two or three basal courses survive (Shinde et al. 2008: 24).
parts.excavator_basis: Cross-dating. The final report dates Period IIA to 2600-2400 BC, IIB to 2400-2200 BC and IIC to 2200-2000 BC and states that 'no radio carbon or AMS dates are yet available', so the ranges rest on 'the cultural materials identified at the site as well as comparative analysis' with other sites (Shinde et al. 2011: 39); the planned town emerged 'in Period-II, around 2600 BC' (p. 40). The 2008 interim report had dated the Mature Harappan phase 'tentatively ... to between 2500-2100 BCE on the basis of seal and sealings and ceramic assemblages', the planned town to 'around 2500 BCE' (Shinde et al. 2008: 15), and the early and late structural phases to c. 2500-2300 and c. 2300-2000 BCE (p. 22).

syntheses.statement: The pottery specialist of the same project reads 'the 13 AMS 14C dates which point to the Harappan period' as ranging 'from 2536 BC (49.6%) 2492 BC (1 σ) to 2346 BC (46.1%) 2278 BC (1σ)', so that 'the occupation in the excavated area at Farmana can be included in the early part of the entire Harappan period (2600 - 1900 BC)' and 'roughly corresponds to Periods 3A and 3B' of Harappa; he finds no clear change in the ceramic assemblage through Phases 1 to 5.
syntheses.disagreement: The excavator's chapters say no radiocarbon dates were available and divide the occupation into Period I (Early Harappan) and Periods IIA-IIB with cross-dated ranges; the AMS dates span only about 2600-2200 BC at two sigma.

syntheses.statement: The project leader's summary states that 'while Prof. Shinde places the earliest levels to the ‘Early Harappan period’ based on his observations, the artefacts, especially pottery coupled with AMS dates from the lower levels point to the ‘Mature’ Harappan period occupation', while allowing that occupation may begin earlier.
syntheses.disagreement: Disputes the excavator's Early Harappan Period I for the lowest excavated levels.

syntheses.statement: 'Based on the stratrigraphy, ceramics and the carbon (AMS) dates, the site was occupied between 2600 and 2200 BCE', 'only during the Mature Harappan Period', for a relatively short time.
syntheses.disagreement: Leaves no room for the excavator's Period I (3500-2600 BC) or Period IIC (2200-2000 BC).

syntheses.statement: The excavator's later regional summary dates periods IIA and IIB together to 2600-2400 BCE and IIC to 2200-1900 BCE 'on the basis of a few accelerator mass spectrometry (AMS) dates' (p. 11), and says 'an extensive horizontal section of period IIB has been unearthed at Farmana, exposing a piece of the perfectly planned Mature Harappan village' (p. 12).
syntheses.disagreement: Assigns the exposed planned area to IIB, as the 2011 descriptions do, and compresses IIA and IIB into 2600-2400 BCE.

parts.conflicts: The phase of the exposed street plan changed between reports: the 2008 interim report puts the 'parallelogram town plan in Locality 1' with Main Street and Lane no. 1 in Structural Phase II, 'Late Period II', c. 2300-2000 BCE (Shinde et al. 2008: 22-23), while the 2011 report says the plan was established in Period IIA and kept unchanged in IIB, yet describes Main Street and Complexes 2-4 under Period IIB. The 2011 report's chronology chapter says no radiocarbon dates were available (p. 39) and announces a list of AMS dates for the Early Harappan levels of Farmana, Girawad and Mitathal that is not printed (p. 38), while chapter 13 of the same volume publishes 21 AMS dates of the Harappan occupation, labelled by stratigraphic Phases 1 to 5 rather than by period. The project's own specialists read the lowest dated levels as Mature Harappan, against the excavator's Early Harappan attribution.

first_occupation.phase: Period I, Early Harappan (Regional Hakra Culture Tradition), called Pre-Harappan in the 2008 interim report; pit-dwellings cut into natural soil, Layers 10-12
first_occupation.basis: Cross-dating with Bhirrana. The final report dates Period I to 3500-2600 BC and says the Early Harappan AMS dates from Farmana, Girawad and Mitathal 'are not consistent and are of limited value', so that it relies on the early dates from Bhirrana to place the beginning 'in the middle of 4th millennium BC' (Shinde et al. 2011: 38). The project's own AMS series and its pottery and botanical specialists place the lowest dated levels in the Mature Harappan period (pp. 254, 813, 839).

notes:
Farmana (Rohtak district) has a habitation mound of about 18 ha and a separate Harappan cemetery; only the habitation's layout concerns us. Deccan College and the Indus Project of the Research Institute for Humanity and Nature (Kyoto) excavated it in 2006-07, 2007-08 and 2008-09. We read the 2007-08 interim report (Occasional Paper 6, 2008) and the final report of 2011, which the Internet Archive holds with a usable text layer. The excavator divides the sequence into Period I (Early Harappan, pit-dwellings) and Period II (Mature Harappan), subdivided into IIA, IIB and IIC, of which IIC has been removed by levelling; separately, the index-trench sections, the AMS chapter and the pottery chapter use stratigraphic Phases 1 to 5, and no table in the report converts one scheme into the other. We therefore list all 21 AMS determinations from the Harappan levels with the phase label they carry, and leave out the four Gupta-period and one late medieval determinations of the same table, which date later pits and fills.

The AMS dates are conventional ages on the 5568-year half-life, calibrated with OxCal 4.1 and IntCal09 (p. 831); none comes from a hearth or oven (p. 254). No Bayesian model has been published. We did not obtain Occasional Paper 3 (Shinde et al. 2008, 'Exploration in the Ghaggar Basin and excavations at Girawad, Farmana (Rohtak District) and Mitathal (Bhiwani District), Haryana, India', pp. 77-158), which reports the 2006-07 season; we searched the Internet Archive and the web without finding a copy. The list of Early Harappan AMS dates announced on p. 38 of the final report is missing from the printed page, so any such dates remain unpublished as far as we know.
